title: Similarity-Constrained Reweighting for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs
claim: Prior methods adjust only the final answer scores with uncalibrated weights; ours applies normalized similarity constraints at any variable in the query.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, separated by vertical dividers, shared query banner on top
description: A gray banner at the top gives the query: 'What are drugs treating diseases that have headache as a symptom?'. Below it, three panels are separated by thin vertical lines. Each panel shows a small path graph that starts at a green 'Headache' node. Arrows lead to gray 'disease' and 'drug' nodes. Under the target node, vertical vectors of grayscale cells represent entity scores. Left: a plain logical query with a single score vector. Middle: the NQR approach. The target score vector is multiplied (⊗) by a blue and red vector, labeled 'similar to Ibuprofen', which gives a tinted result vector. The red and blue colors mark the uncalibrated adjustments. Right: SCORE. The constraint 'similar to Migraine' is applied at the intermediate disease node, multiplied with a normalized grayscale vector, and the adjusted scores then propagate to the drug node. The eye goes first to the colored vectors in the middle panel.
caption: Illustration of three approaches for query answering on knowledge graphs, with vectors indicating entity scores at different steps. Left: a traditional query with purely logical constraints. Middle: incorporating similarity constraints in NQR [ref], which supports only the target variable via uncalibrated score adjustments (shown in red and blue). Right: SCORE, which supports similarity constraints on arbitrary variables through normalized similarity scores.
abstract: Machine learning models for Complex Query Answering (CQA) on knowledge graphs estimate the likelihood of answers that are not reachable via direct traversal. Recent work has proposed extending such queries with soft entity constraints, which require the target variable to be similar or dissimilar to specified sets of entities. We study a more general formulation where similarity constraints are specified on an arbitrary variable in a query, and introduce SCORE: a computationally efficient and interpretable method for incorporating similarity constraints on an arbitrary variable of a query. SCORE is based on a lightweight and interpretable score adjustment function that only requires tuning two hyperparameters on a validation set. Our experiments show that SCORE effectively incorporates preferences while maintaining strong query answering performance. It significantly improves ranking quality when constraints apply to the target variable and performs effectively in the more general case involving constraints on intermediate variables, and its performance remains robust when applied to several existing methods for CQA. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/dfdazac/score.
